newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania c.bank to issue leu rate computing method.
newsitem.headline: Romania c.bank to issue leu rate computing method.

text.p: Romania's central bank (BNR) said on Friday it would soon announce a new method of computing the reference exchange rates for the leu currency.
"The National Bank wanted to test how the local foreign exchange market reacted when the bank no longer computed the reference rate," a BNR official said.
"We probed into dealers' capacity to work in independent conditions, free from the anchor of the BNR's reference rate," said Ion Dragulin, head of BNR's monetary policy department.
Two weeks ago, the BNR said it would no longer compute the reference rate for the leu.
A later statement said the BNR's latest reference rate of 7,744 lei to the dollar, computed on February 19, would remain in force until a new method was worked out.
Earlier this month, the BNR restored local dealer licences to 24 banks, which, together with the previous four licensed leaders, now act as market makers.

The reference rate, computed since August 1994 when the BNR introduced a free-floating foreign exchange market, was a weighted average based on daily reports of market operators. It was a guidance rate used for statistical accounting purposes.

Dealers' quotes displayed by banks showed a variety of ranges over the past week, in contrast with the one-rate policy imposed by the four dealers. On Friday, dealers' quotes ranged from 6,800/900 to 8,000/100 against the dollar.
